findings.summary: This bounded usability follow-up changes only the four granted CODEX-06-A files (LoopPlayer.tsx, loop-player.css, the invented fixture's opening string and the existing player tests). It adds a static inline SVG with a fixed-size block whose position is the only variable. The tilt and outcome come only from the engine's validated `current_result` or a retained trial, and neither is shown before Test. I checked the engine: both configure and predict clear `current_result`, and Test resets `configuration`, so there is no stale or early reveal. The real React/jsdom test checks the block moving, the outcome staying unresolved until Test, the tilt appearing only after Test, two retained visual tries, and the grown-up notes starting collapsed. Together with the controller's reported 20/20 tests, build and protected `check_application_card` results, this supports all three card criteria. No browser or layout claim is made from jsdom, and nothing widens policy, packaging, deployment, the engine or the data scope.

findings.title: Retained-try SVGs duplicate the dl text for screen readers
findings.problem: Each retained try now has a compact `<svg role="img" aria-label="Block in the middle. Stayed steady.">` plus a figcaption with the same position and result, followed by the dl that repeats the position and result again. Screen-reader users hear each try's position and result about three times, which makes comparing two tries tedious. The accessibility goal for this follow-up is meaningful image labels, not repeated announcements. It does not break a card criterion.
findings.fix_check: Mark the compact trial SVG and its figcaption as decorative (`aria-hidden`), or drop the duplicate dl rows, so the accessibility tree announces each try's guess, position and result once. A reviewer can confirm this in the DOM test or in the browser accessibility tree.

findings.title: New test does not assert the collapsed limits text stays complete
findings.problem: The follow-up says the complete limits must stay available after they move into a collapsed `<details>`. The new test only checks that `details.open === false`. The protected probe only matches /synthetic|toy/i anywhere on the page. Neither check confirms that the `<details>` holds the full `adventure.limits` text or that the 'Synthetic toy preview · unreviewed' label is still visible outside it. The code does render both correctly today.
findings.fix_check: Add assertions that `details p` textContent equals `fixtureAdventure.limits` and that `.loop-player-label` sits outside `<details>` and contains 'unreviewed'.

findings.title: Dead aside CSS left after limits moved into details
findings.problem: `.loop-player aside` and `.loop-player aside h2` no longer match anything, because the only `<aside>` was replaced by `<details>`.
findings.fix_check: Remove the two aside rules, or reuse them for `.loop-player-limits`.

findings.title: Test writes its transpiled module into the app/ source directory
findings.problem: The test writes `app/.visual-test-<uuid>.mjs` into the source tree. The `wx` flag and the cleanup in `finally` are correct, but if the process is killed mid-run a stray file is left in app/. A temp directory or a path under tests/ would be safer, provided relative imports still resolve.
findings.fix_check: Leftover-file risk is accepted or documented. Otherwise, write the file under tests/ or a dedicated ignored directory and rewrite its relative imports.

findings.title: Browser and phone check of the new visual is still pending
findings.problem: The SVG sizing (`width: min(100%, 27rem)`, compact `max-width: 13rem`, auto-fit trial grid) looks phone-safe in code, but jsdom proves no layout. As the task states, a real-browser QA of this visual version is separate and has not been done. This review does not count as that check, approve the science or learning content, or promote any task status.
findings.fix_check: A separate real-browser run at a narrow phone width and a desktop width records the setup, the tilt appearing only after Test, and two retained visual tries.
